text: dsh-session-recap 是 DSH Web 会话回顾插件：用户离开一段时间后，它根据会话进度生成简短摘要，并在返回时显示在输入框上方。插件跟踪 Web 客户端状态和已完成回合，在满足空闲时长、回合数和文本量条件时调用会话可用的模型路由；也可通过 /recap 手动生成。摘要包含当前任务、关键进展和下一步，保存在插件侧车文件中，不写入会话消息。适合需要离开后快速恢复工作上下文的 DSH 用户；自动回顾需要 Web 客户端和可用模型路由。

dsh-session-recap adds short away recaps to DSH Web sessions. After idle and conversation thresholds are met, it summarizes the task, progress, and next action using the session model route. The recap appears above the composer when you return; /recap also creates one on demand.
想在回到 DSH 时看到离开期间的会话进展摘要。
让 DSH 在我离开一段时间后自动总结当前任务和下一步。
有没有办法手动生成当前会话的简短回顾？
我切回一个会话时，想在输入框旁快速看上次的进度。
Can DSH summarize a session after I have been away for a while?
I want a short recap of the current task and next step when I return to my session.
How can I request a session recap manually from the slash menu?
**dsh-session-recap** 的功能「自动离开回顾」：当所有已连接的 Web 客户端持续处于离开状态，且会话达到空闲时长、已完成回合数和文本量门槛时，插件调用模型生成摘要；回顾展示当前任务、重要进展和下一步。
**dsh-session-recap** 的功能「手动生成回顾」：用户可从 Web 斜杠菜单运行 /recap，按需为当前会话生成摘要；也可启用 hostCommand，在没有 Web 客户端的 profile 中注册主机命令。
**dsh-session-recap** 的功能「返回会话查看摘要」：插件将当前回顾显示在会话输入框上方，用户可以关闭提示；客户端轮询主机端点获取会话快照。
**dsh-session-recap** 的功能「摘要持久化与长度控制」：主机将摘要保存到插件数据目录的侧车文件，并对输入 transcript 字节数、模型输出 token 和最终摘要字符数设上限。
dsh-session-recap 使用会话当前可用的模型路由生成摘要，并把 transcript 内容发送给该模型；需要确保会话模型路由可用。固定路由可同时配置 provider 和 model。
I need a compact summary of what happened while I was away from a coding session.

@dsh-external/dsh-session-recap README · Summary：This bundle adds away recaps to a DeepSeek Harness session. When every Web client connected to the host has explicitly been away for at least `idleMs`, the last completed turn is also older than `idleMs`, and the session reaches both `minTurns` and `minConversationChars`, the host asks an auxiliary model for a short plain-text recap and stores it in a plugin sidecar. The Web client shows that recap above the composer when the user returns, with the current task, the important progress, and the next action. `/recap` also generates one on demand, and `hostCommand: true` exposes the same command to profiles that have no Web client.

@dsh-external/dsh-session-recap README · Table of Contents：- [Install](#install) - [Use this package](#use-this-package) - [Configure](#configure) - [Understand the implementation](#understand-the-implementation) - [Further Exploration](#further-exploration) - [Model Experience](#model-experience) - [Known Limitations and Deferred Work](#known-limitations-and-deferred-work) - [Dev Note](#dev-note) -----

@dsh-external/dsh-session-recap README · Install：Install from GitHub into a profile.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:DDDFXYqiming/dsh-session-recap
```

A git install runs the package `prepare` script and rebuilds `lib/`. pnpm 10 and newer refuse that build until the profile allows it, so the first `add` can fail. Copy the exact package key pnpm prints into the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, then run `add` again.

```yaml
allowBuilds:
  '@dsh-external/dsh-session-recap': true
```

@dsh-external/dsh-session-recap README · Install：That permission lets the package run code on your machine during install. Pin a commit (`github:DDDFXYqiming/dsh-session-recap#<sha>`) if the repository may change. A tarball produced by `pnpm pack` installs without a build.

To install from a local checkout, build it first and point `add` at the directory.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/DDDFXYqiming/dsh-session-recap.git
cd dsh-session-recap
npm install && npm run build
dsh plugin --profile web add .

@dsh-external/dsh-session-recap README · Use this package：When you return to a session, a recap card above the composer shows the current task, the most important progress point, and the next action. The × button closes it. The card disappears when the session advances, and a session keeps one current recap.

@dsh-external/dsh-session-recap README · Use this package：Automatic recaps cover interactive sessions you have visited. Every WebUI page must explicitly remain away for at least `idleMs`; the last completed turn must also be at least `idleMs` old, the session must have at least `minTurns` completed turns, and real user/assistant text must contain at least `minConversationChars` non-whitespace characters. Tool results and injected content do not count. Focusing any WebUI page cancels scheduled and in-flight automatic recaps across all sessions. Switching sessions within the focused application keeps it active. Starting a new turn cancels that session's generation and clears its previous recap.

@dsh-external/dsh-session-recap README · Use this package：Clients send a heartbeat every 20 seconds. An active client whose 45-second lease expires becomes unknown, and automatic recaps pause until that client reports an explicit state again.

To generate a recap at any time, run `/recap` from the slash menu. Profiles without a Web client set `hostCommand: true` and receive the recap text from the host command instead of the card.

The recap follows the language of your own messages, not the language of pasted logs or quoted material.

@dsh-external/dsh-session-recap README · Use this package：

@dsh-external/dsh-session-recap README · Configure：The bundle default row needs no configuration. To change a value, add an entry for `dsh-session-recap` to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. Unset keys take the schema defaults below.

```yaml
- id: dsh-session-recap
  config:
    enabled: true           # Automatic recaps. /recap stays available when false.
    hostCommand: false      # Register the host /recap command. Set true only without a Web client.

@dsh-external/dsh-session-recap README · Configure：`provider` and `model` work as a pair. Leave both empty to reuse the provider and model from the session's last logged request. A recap route that uses a thinking model spends `maxOutputTokens` on thinking tokens too; if the first attempt produces no complete sentence, the plugin retries once with `min(4096, max(2048, maxOutputTokens × 4))` tokens. `manualRequestTimeoutMs` bounds only the browser's wait for a manual request; generation continues on the host and a later poll updates the card.

@dsh-external/dsh-session-recap README · Understand the implementation：Input framing keeps the conversation and drops tool output. The frame takes the last `recentMessages` messages from the assistant and from real user input, drops tool results and injected context, uses the newest compaction checkpoint as trusted history, and adds the newest user request as `goal` when it has fallen outside the window. The JSON frame is trimmed to the `maxInputChars` byte budget by shortening its longest strings.

@dsh-external/dsh-session-recap README · Understand the implementation：Generation is one auxiliary model call with a fixed system prompt and one user message. The system prompt asks for two to four plain sentences, restates the `maxChars` hard limit, forbids Markdown, and orders the content as current task, one important progress point or decision, and one next action. The user message carries the JSON frame plus a `[recap-language]` directive with up to three recent user messages, so the model writes in the language the user writes in. The reply is cleaned of reasoning tags and Markdown, clipped to `maxChars`, and reduced to complete sentences when a cut lands mid-sentence.

@dsh-external/dsh-session-recap README · Understand the implementation：The host stores and serves the text. A sidecar file at `$DSH_HOME/plugin-data/dsh-session-recap/<encoded-session-id>.json` stores `text`, `at`, and `turnSeq`, written through a temporary file and rename. The in-memory copy is served by `GET /api/dsh-session-recap?sessionId=...`; the Web client polls it, renders the card in the `conversation.input.dock` slot, and remembers a dismissal in `sessionStorage` for that session, turn, and timestamp. The route accepts `GET`, `HEAD`, and `POST` for presence or a manual generation request.

@dsh-external/dsh-session-recap README · Understand the implementation：The route answers local callers only. The remote address must be a loopback address, the `Host` header must match an anchored loopback pattern, `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` is refused, and a missing `Origin` is allowed while a present one must parse and its host must equal `Host`. Setting `routeProbe: true` writes allow and deny verdicts to `route-probe.log` in the plugin data directory for diagnosis. -----

@dsh-external/dsh-session-recap README · Further Exploration：

@dsh-external/dsh-session-recap README · What the model sees：One recap call sends a fixed system prompt and one user message. The system prompt asks for two to four plain sentences in the user's language, restates the `maxChars` hard limit, forbids Markdown and label-colon outlines, and orders the content as current task, one important progress point or decision, and one next action. The user message carries the JSON transcript frame `{ historySummary, goal, recent }` and a `[recap-language]` directive built from up to three recent user messages. `historySummary` is the newest compaction checkpoint, `goal` is the newest real user request when it fell outside the window, and `recent` holds role-labelled conversation entries.

@dsh-external/dsh-session-recap README · Token effect：The plugin adds one independent request per automatic trigger or manual `/recap`. The transcript is capped at `maxInputChars` bytes (24000 by default), and `recentMessages` (80 by default) bounds how many messages enter the frame. Output is capped at `maxOutputTokens` (2048 by default), with one retry at `min(4096, max(2048, maxOutputTokens × 4))` when the first attempt returns no complete sentence. The recap text is clipped to `maxChars` (400 by default) characters and never enters the session's model input or message history.

@dsh-external/dsh-session-recap README · KV Cache effect：Each recap is an independent single-turn request. Its transcript changes with the session, so there is no stable prefix to reuse between recaps. The plugin does not modify session messages, the session system prompt, or tool definitions, so the session's own request prefix stays reusable.

@dsh-external/dsh-session-recap README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **Automatic recaps need a Web client.** Away detection depends on client presence. A profile without a Web client gets `/recap` only when `hostCommand: true`, and never generates a recap on its own.
- **A model route must be available.** The host uses the explicit `provider` and `model` pair, or the route from the session's last logged request. With neither, generation fails and the host logs a warning.
- **Thinking routes consume the output budget.** Reasoning tokens count against `maxOutputTokens`. A small budget can return no complete sentence; the single escalated retry may still fail, and `/recap` then reports the error.
- **Teammate and subagent sessions stay manual.** A session with a parent session never arms an automatic recap, so a teammate conversation generates one only through `/recap`.
- **The route answers loopback clients only.** A remote or LAN caller cannot read a recap from the host route, even with the right session id.
- **Dismissals are per browser tab.** The Web client records a dismissal in `sessionStorage`, and another tab does not inherit it.

<summary>Working context for maintainers — click to expand</summary>

Keep `routeProbe` off outside diagnosis. It appends synchronously on the route, and a polling client can hit the disk on every request. The escalation factor, 2048 floor, and 4096 ceiling in `generateRecap` are fixed strategy constants, not config values. Run `npm run build` and `npm test` before publishing.

</details>
